newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Confusion reigns over Venezuela shipping ruling.
newsitem.headline: Confusion reigns over Venezuela shipping ruling.

text.p: A regional Venezuelan judge threw the country's oil industry into confusion when he banned single-hulled tankers from using the Lake Maracaibo shipping channel, the route used for over a million barrels per day (bpd) of Venezuelan crude oil exports.

Only about 20 percent of the world's tanker fleet has double- hulls or double-bottoms, shipping sources say, so the ruling, if implemented, would drastically increase the cost of transporting crude and therefore reduce the price Venezuela fetches for it.
A source at state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) said the company was taken by surprise by the decision and was hoping to talk to the judge, and probably appeal the decision, very soon.

"He took the decision without considering how many double- bottom ships there are in the world or the consequence it could have on the market... I think he will have to reconsider for the good of everyone," the source said.
Judge Ricardo Colmenares made the ruling following a 25,000 barrel oil spill from the single-hulled Nissos Amorgos tanker, which hit bottom in the Lake Maracaibo shipping channel on February 28.
Only two weeks later, on March 10, the double-hulled Olympic Sponsor went aground in the same spot as the Nissos, but its second skin prevented any spill, shipping sources say.
Currently, PDVSA owns 12 double-hulled tankers which would be able to handle about 400,000 bpd exports from the Lake Maracaibo, or 40 percent of current levels, shipping sources say.

The level of confusion was illustrated by a Minsitry of Transport spokesman who, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Reuters: "Venezuela will present no hindrance in its waters to ships with a single hull. Venezuela is signatory to the IMO (International Maritime Organisation) agreements and specifically MARPOL (an international agreement for the prevention of pollution from ships)."
But he added: "This is a measure taken by a judge of the Republic and there are ways for the people affected by these measures to appeal within the judicial system."
The MARPOL agreement calls for all tankers over 25 years old to be double-hulled, but it allows single-skin tankers under 25 years old to trade with MARPOL countries.
In his ruling, Judge Colmenares said the ban would take effect on April 16.
A PDVSA source said: "At the moment PDVSA is studying all its options and will act as soon as possible because this affects the whole country."
